blocks.text: Leica Camera AG honours the Mexican photographer Graciela Iturbide by presenting her with the 2026 Leica Hall of Fame Award.

She is the world’s most famous contemporary Mexican photographer: this year, Graciela Iturbide was awarded the ‘Leica Hall of Fame’ prize in recognition of her life’s work. The award ceremony took place as part of the ‘Celebration of Photography’ on 8 October 2026 at Leica World in Wetzlar. The accompanying exhibition, featuring more than 50 photographs, will be on display at the Leica Gallery in Wetzlar until January 2027. Iturbide’s photograph ‘Na’ Lupe Pan’, from the series ‘Juchitán’, Oaxaca, Mexico, 1986, was voted ‘Leica Photo of the Year 2026’. The exhibition offers an in-depth insight into the artist’s work, which is primarily devoted to Latin American cultural history. Exploring universal themes such as life and death, rituals and everyday experiences, Iturbide’s visual world is characterised by its moving poetry and magic. The photographer highlights the tensions between culture and nature, tradition and modernity, identity and representation, ensuring that her images retain an enigmatic ambiguity. Deeply rooted in indigenous Mexican culture and blending surrealist elements with religion and mysticism, Graciela Iturbide has, over many decades, developed an inimitable visual language – predominantly in black and white. Birds and masks appear time and again as symbolic companions. The photographer’s most famous work, the astonishing ‘Nuestra Señora de las iguanas’ (Our Lady of the Iguanas), was taken in 1979 at a market in Juchitán. It is a mysterious portrait of a market vendor wearing a crown of live iguanas: a Mexican hydra, but also, according to Christian interpretation, a female figure of Christ wearing a crown of thorns with an animalistic character. Graciela Iturbide’s photographic work is part of a humanist tradition that incorporates psychological and spiritual elements, transforming the documentary image into a form of subjective photography that is extraordinarily rich in nuance. In addition to her still lifes and landscapes, it is her social reportage on the living conditions of Mexico’s indigenous communities and on the importance of matriarchal social structures that has caused a sensation and established her as one of Latin America’s most important photographic voices. The exhibition, organised to coincide with the presentation of the Leica Hall of Fame Award, brings together more than 50 photographs from five series: ‘Juchitán’, featuring images of this Mexican city in the state of Oaxaca (1979–1988); ‘México Clásicas’ (1974–2008); ‘Pájaros ’ (Birds, 1987–1998), ‘Desierto de Sonora’ (1979) and ‘Viajes’ (Travels), taken in Ecuador, Panama, Argentina and Cuba (1972–1994).

Graciela Iturbide was born in Mexico City on 16 May 1942. Even as a child, she was fascinated by photography: her father was a keen amateur photographer. She married the architect Manuel Rocha Díaz (1936–1996) at the age of 19 and went on to have three children. In 1969, she began studying film at the Colegio Nacional de México, at the Centro Universitario de Estudios Cinematográficos (CUEC). In 1970, she spent a year as an assistant to the photographer Manuel Álvarez Bravo, accompanying him on numerous trips and thereby discovering rural Mexico and the diversity of its indigenous communities. A twist of fate – the death of her six-year-old daughter Cláudia – radically changed Graciela Iturbide’s life, leading her to decide to become a professional photographer. In 1975, she held her first exhibition in Mexico City, followed by her first in New York in 1976. From the 1980s onwards, she began to gain international recognition. She has received numerous awards, including the W. Eugene Smith Prize (1987), the Hugo Erfurth Prize (1989), the Rencontres Internationales de la Photographie d’Arles Prize (1991), the Hasselblad Award (2008), the Gold Medal from the Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes y Literatura (INBAL) in Mexico City (2024) and the Princess of Asturias Award for the Arts (2025). Iturbide lives in Mexico City.
